_comment: Scoring rubric for the Releases channel. These are STARTING DEFAULTS and are expected to be wrong: the brief says so explicitly (§12.2). The way to fix the channel's volume is to change a number in this file, never to reword a prompt — a prompt change is unmeasurable and a threshold change is not. Run the channel in --dry-run for a week, read the score distribution out of state/queue.json and state/rejected.jsonl, and raise `threshold` until the output is the eight-a-week the budget targets.
_comment_tier1: Tier-1 vendors (brief §14.4). A tier-1 release scores +1 (tier1_vendor). The file used to say this was the number most likely to be wrong, and it was: `non_tier1` (-2) applied to EVERYTHING that was not tier-1, including every lab this tracker deliberately follows. Combined with a vendor field that never normalised (fixed in core/classify.py), it charged -2 on OpenAI's and Anthropic's own announcements and the channel published nothing for a month. The penalty now means what it says — an UNKNOWN lab — and the labs we chose to track sit at 0 in `watched_vendors` below.
_comment_watched: Labs this tracker follows on purpose: neither credited like a tier-1 vendor nor penalised like an unknown one. The test for membership is simple — if a lab has a source in feeds-releases.json, we decided it mattered, so it belongs here. Without this, an open-weights release from one of them needed open_weights (+2) AND a benchmark claim just to reach the bar: 'Kimi K3 by Moonshot AI is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock' scored 4 of 6 and was dropped.
_comment_age: A release is news for about a fortnight. Several sources here are back CATALOGUES rather than feeds — every Hugging Face org endpoint hands back thirty repositories whether they landed this morning or in 2023 — so an age filter, not just a seen-before check, is what keeps history out of the candidate pool. Found by the Phase 3 dry run, which without it enqueued OpenAI's 2023 diffusion checkpoints as new model releases.
_comment_volume: Two high-volume feeds need filtering before scoring or they drown the candidate pool in unrelated product news (brief §12.1d): Microsoft's Azure updates feed carries all of Azure, and AWS What's New carries all of AWS. An item from one of these is only considered when its title or summary mentions one of the families below.
